title: Ion charges card
subject: Science (GCSE Biology, Chemistry, Physics)
source: Seeded from gcse-science/y10 lesson 105 (Ion charges card (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 105: Formulae and balanced equations. To understand how to write formulae and balanced symbol equations with state symbols

keywords.def: symbols showing the atoms in a substance and their ratio
the big number in front of a formula in an equation
the small number in a formula, never changed when balancing
atoms are not created or destroyed in reactions

questions.model: Oxygen: 2 on the left, 1 on the right: put 2 in front of Na₂O. Now 4 Na on the right: put 4 in front of Na. Check: 4 Na, 2 O each side.

questions.q: Write the formula of calcium nitrate.
Core: Balance eight equations (portal worksheet), e.g. H₂ + Cl₂ → HCl; Fe + O₂ → Fe₂O₃; CaCO₃ + HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂.
questions.a: H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl; 4Fe + 3O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃; CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂; others in the key.
questions.model: Teacher balances the first: H₂ + Cl₂ → HCl has 2 H and 2 Cl on the left, so 2HCl on the right.

questions.q: Extend: Write a balanced equation with state symbols for magnesium burning in oxygen. [2 marks]
questions.a: 2Mg(s) + O₂(g) → 2MgO(s): formulae (1), balancing and state symbols (1).

questions.q: Stretch: Write a balanced equation for sodium reacting with water to form sodium hydroxide solution and hydrogen.
Big question: why must every chemical equation balance?
questions.a: Atoms are not created or destroyed, so each element must have the same number of atoms on both sides.
